cond_0001.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Nurse RN to join our team.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
What You Will Do**
To provide direct and indirect nursing services to patients and families.
Essential Functions**
Clinical advancement: Uses systematic planning, appropriate methods and timely exchange of information with multidisciplinary team and patient/family to coordinate care. Demonstrates ability to focus on and manage multiple patient needs and aspects of care. Actively communicates with care team to plan patient care. Utilizes available resources to problem-solve and determine most effective approach to action.
Clinical judgment and decision making: Utilizes the nursing process and a critical thinking approach to provide patient care that incorporates the mind, body and spirit; is individualized, goal directed, and consistent with current standards of safety. Identifies actual/potential problems for which the patient is at risk. Continuously evaluates interventions and care, and adjusts the plan as patient and family needs change. Identifies need for referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Collaborates with patient, family and other team members to develop a comprehensive plan of care. Prioritizes demand for resources and collaborates with others to meet individualized patient needs. Acts as preceptor/teacher in guiding other nurses on how to apply the nursing process with a particular unit population. Makes appropriate referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Implements safe, therapeutic and efficient care for patients with complex needs due to multi-system disease and/or complications of treatment. Demonstrates accountability for achieving patient outcomes. Demonstrates an ability to quickly recognize a patient diagnosis even though presenting symptoms or situations may be dissimilar. Documents per department/entity guidelines of care and policies and procedures. Comprehensive; representing detailed, concise picture of patient's care. Serves as a resource for other staff in managing unit specific documentation issues. Charting reflects a critical thinking/problem oriented approach to patient issues.
Clinical leadership: Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Knowledgeable about what can and cannot be delegated to each different health care team member. Responsible for delegation and follows through to ensure delegated task is complete. Before delegating, analyzes each situation, determines and consistently applies levels of supervision needed (unsupervised, initial direction and periodic inspection, continuous supervision, or should not be delegated). Assesses appropriateness of physician orders and to question physician when appropriate. Helps coworkers improve performance. Offers assistance and support to coworkers. Provides positive feedback to others. Provides unit specific information to students, floats, travelers/registry personnel and documents appropriately. Provides incidental teaching to members of the team. Looks for and applies ways to improve work processes and systems. Offers and accepts constructive feedback/criticism in a non-judgmental, positive and confidential manner. Seeks out opportunities to assist and support coworkers.
Nurse-patient/family relationship: Establishes a therapeutic relationship with patient and family. Anticipates problems to establishing/maintaining a therapeutic relationship with a specific patient and takes actions to enhance quality of nurse/patient/family interaction (problems may include: spiritual, cultural, language or other communication barriers; those imposed by nature of illness or health issue). Analyzes social/cultural variables and adapts nursing interventions to meet diverse needs. Serves as a patient advocate through actions such as: removing obstacles, identifying and supporting appropriate needs and wants; interpreting for patient to physician and visa/versa. Provides age appropriate patient education that facilitates recovery, self-care, end-of-life care and health maintenance, health promotion, and wellness. Coordinates transfer and discharge planning and teaching in collaboration with other members of the health care team. Collaborates with other team members to identify, develop and/or revise patient education materials. Demonstrates flexibility to teaching based on assessment of learner's needs and the integration of adult learning principles.
Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities**
Independently performs the nursing process through individualized assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of safe, therapeutic, efficient care for patients with overt and subtle needs throughout the continuum of care, and according to unit's standards of care. Performs safe nursing care for patients in more complex situations with some assistance and supervision. Demonstrates competency in all areas of the unit skills and some advanced skills. May teach some skills competencies. Coordinates patient care administered by other members of the care team. May assume the responsibility of relief charge nurse and may assist with preceptorship/professional development of new nurses and students. Uses common equipment and medications safely in the practice setting and consults others when unfamiliar. Recognizes inconsistencies in patient care and manages potential complications. Demonstrates consistent organization and prioritization of workload; confident management of emergency situations. Participates in quality improvement initiatives. Complies with all regulatory and accreditation standards. Demonstrates professional behavior through participation in unit activities and committees as appropriate. Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Teaches skills as necessary. Coordinates patient care administered by other members of the nursing staff. Utilizes a variety of teaching/coaching strategies to assist family through disease process/experience. Promotes clinical effectiveness, efficient use of resources, and quality care in practice setting. Transfers knowledge and mentors others to improve clinical practice. Demonstrates complex problem solving and the use of critical thinking skills.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements**
Graduate of nursing school
California Registered Nurse (RN) - CA Board of Registered Nursing
AHA Basic Life Support for Healthcare Professional (AHA BLS Healthcare) - American Heart Association
NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS) - Various-Employee provides certificate (required within 90 days of hire)
1 Year clinical experience (RNs with less than 12 months experience will complete the new grad requirements)
Preferred Requirements**
1 Or more years of related hospital clinical RN hospital patient care experience

cond_0006.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Nurse RN to join our team.
cond_0006.responsibilities:
Clinical advancement
Stays in regular contact with the multidisciplinary team and patient/family to coordinate care using systematic planning, appropriate methods, and timely exchange of information. Actively communicates with the care team throughout the day to plan and adjust patient care. Manages multiple patient needs at once and connects with available resources to determine the most effective approach.
Clinical judgment and decision making
Applies the nursing process and critical thinking to provide individualized, goal-directed patient care consistent with current safety standards. Identifies actual and potential problems, continuously evaluates interventions, and adjusts the plan as patient and family needs change. Collaborates daily with patients, families, and team members to develop and maintain a comprehensive care plan. Initiates referrals based on initial and ongoing assessments. Implements safe, therapeutic, and efficient care for patients with complex, multi-system needs. Maintains thorough, concise documentation that reflects a critical thinking approach and serves as a resource for other staff on documentation issues.
Clinical leadership
Delegates and clearly communicates care delivery expectations to each team member. Analyzes each situation before delegating and applies the appropriate level of supervision. Questions physician orders when appropriate and actively supports coworkers by offering assistance, positive feedback, and constructive input. Shares unit-specific information with students, float staff, and travelers. Looks for ways to improve work processes and brings those ideas forward to the team.
Nurse-patient/family relationship
Builds and maintains a therapeutic relationship with patients and families, anticipating barriers such as cultural, spiritual, language, or illness-related challenges and taking steps to address them. cond_0018.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Nurse RN to join our team.
cond_0018.responsibilities:
Essential Functions**
Clinical advancement: Coordinates care through systematic planning, appropriate methods, and timely exchange of information with the multidisciplinary team and patient/family. Works alongside the care team to manage multiple patient needs and aspects of care. Actively shares updates with the care team to plan patient care. Works with available resources to determine the most effective approach to action.
Clinical judgment and decision making: Applies the nursing process and critical thinking to provide patient care that incorporates the mind, body, and spirit; individualized, goal directed, and consistent with current safety standards. Identifies actual/potential problems for which the patient is at risk. Continuously evaluates interventions and care, and adjusts the plan as patient and family needs change. Identifies need for referrals based on initial and ongoing assessments. Collaborates with the patient, family, and team members to develop a comprehensive plan of care. Works with others to prioritize resources and meet individualized patient needs. Supports other nurses by helping them apply the nursing process with a particular unit population. Makes appropriate referrals based on assessments and evaluation. Helps ensure safe, therapeutic, and efficient care for patients with complex needs due to multi-system disease and/or complications of treatment. Shares accountability for achieving patient outcomes. Recognizes patient diagnoses even when presenting symptoms or situations may differ. Documents per department/entity guidelines, policies, and procedures in a detailed, concise manner. Supports other staff in managing unit-specific documentation issues. Charting reflects a critical thinking and problem-oriented approach.
Clinical leadership: Coordinates and communicates expectations for care delivery processes with each member of the team. Understands what can and cannot be delegated to each health care team member. Follows through to ensure delegated tasks are complete. Before delegating, analyzes each situation and applies appropriate levels of supervision. Assesses appropriateness of physician orders and raises questions when appropriate. Helps coworkers improve performance. Offers assistance and support to coworkers. Provides positive feedback to others. Shares unit-specific information with students, floats, and travelers/registry personnel and documents appropriately. Provides incidental teaching to team members. Looks for and applies ways to improve work processes and systems. Offers and accepts constructive feedback in a non-judgmental, positive, and confidential manner.
Nurse-patient/family relationship: Establishes a therapeutic relationship with patient and family. Anticipates barriers to maintaining a therapeutic relationship and takes actions to improve the quality of nurse/patient/family interaction (barriers may include spiritual, cultural, language, or other communication issues; or those related to the nature of illness). Adapts nursing interventions to meet diverse needs based on social/cultural variables. Serves as a patient advocate by removing obstacles, identifying and supporting appropriate needs and wants, and interpreting between patient and physician. Provides age-appropriate patient education to support recovery, self-care, end-of-life care, health maintenance, health promotion, and wellness. Coordinates transfer and discharge planning and teaching in collaboration with other members of the health care team. Works with team members to identify, develop, and/or revise patient education materials. Adapts teaching based on assessment of learner needs and adult learning principles.
cond_0018.requirements:
Graduate of nursing school. 1 Year clinical experience (RNs with less than 12 months experience will complete the new grad requirements). California Registered Nurse (RN) - CA Board of Registered Nursing - REQUIRED. AHA Basic Life Support for Healthcare Professional (AHA BLS Healthcare) - American Heart Association - REQUIRED. NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS) - Various-Employee provides certificate - REQUIRED. NIHSS is required within 90 days of hire. 1 Or more years of related hospital clinical RN hospital patient care experience.
Independently performs the nursing process through individualized assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation of safe, therapeutic, efficient care for patients with overt and subtle needs throughout the continuum of care, and according to unit standards of care. Performs safe nursing care for patients in more complex situations with some assistance and supervision. Demonstrates competency in all areas of unit skills and some advanced skills. May teach some skills competencies. Coordinates patient care administered by other members of the care team. May assume the responsibility of relief charge nurse and may assist with preceptorship/professional development of new nurses and students. Uses common equipment and medications safely in the practice setting and consults others when unfamiliar. Recognizes inconsistencies in patient care and manages potential complications. Demonstrates consistent organization and prioritization of workload; confident management of emergency situations. Participates in quality improvement initiatives. Complies with all regulatory and accreditation standards. Demonstrates professional behavior through participation in unit activities and committees as appropriate. Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Teaches skills as necessary. Coordinates patient care administered by other members of the nursing staff. Utilizes a variety of teaching/coaching strategies to assist family through disease process/experience. Promotes clinical effectiveness, efficient use of resources, and quality care in practice setting. Transfers knowledge and mentors others to improve clinical practice. Demonstrates complex problem solving and the use of critical thinking skills.

cond_0069.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Nurse RN to join our team.
cond_0069.responsibilities:
Clinical advancement
Uses systematic planning, appropriate methods, and regular exchange of information with the multidisciplinary team and patient/family to coordinate care. Actively communicates with the care team daily to plan patient care. Demonstrates ability to focus on and manage multiple patient needs and aspects of care. Utilizes available resources to problem-solve and determine the most effective approach.
Clinical judgment and decision making
Utilizes the nursing process and a critical thinking approach to provide patient care that incorporates the mind, body, and spirit; is individualized, goal directed, and consistent with current standards of safety. Identifies actual/potential problems for which the patient is at risk. Continuously evaluates interventions and care, and adjusts the plan as patient and family needs change. Identifies need for referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Collaborates closely with the patient, family, and other team members to develop a comprehensive plan of care. Prioritizes demand for resources and works with others to meet individualized patient needs. Acts as preceptor/teacher in guiding other nurses on how to apply the nursing process with a particular unit population. Implements safe, therapeutic, and efficient care for patients with complex needs due to multi-system disease and/or complications of treatment. Demonstrates accountability for achieving patient outcomes. Demonstrates an ability to quickly recognize a patient diagnosis even though presenting symptoms or situations may be dissimilar. Documents per department/entity guidelines of care and policies and procedures; charting reflects a critical thinking/problem-oriented approach to patient issues. Serves as a resource for other staff in managing unit-specific documentation issues.
Clinical leadership
Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Knowledgeable about what can and cannot be delegated to each different health care team member. Responsible for delegation and follows through to ensure delegated tasks are complete. Before delegating, analyzes each situation and consistently applies appropriate levels of supervision. Assesses appropriateness of physician orders and speaks up to question the physician when appropriate. Helps coworkers improve performance. Offers assistance and support to coworkers. Provides positive feedback to others. Provides unit-specific information to students, floats, and travelers/registry personnel. Provides incidental teaching to members of the team. Looks for and applies ways to improve work processes and systems. Offers and accepts constructive feedback in a non-judgmental, positive, and confidential manner.
Nurse-patient/family relationship
Establishes a therapeutic relationship with patients and families through regular, ongoing interaction. Anticipates problems in establishing or maintaining a therapeutic relationship and takes actions to enhance the quality of nurse/patient/family interaction. Analyzes social/cultural variables and adapts nursing interventions to meet diverse needs. Serves as a patient advocate by removing obstacles, identifying and supporting appropriate needs and wants, and interpreting between patient and physician. Provides age-appropriate patient education that facilitates recovery, self-care, end-of-life care, and health maintenance. Coordinates transfer and discharge planning and teaching in collaboration with other members of the health care team. Collaborates with other team members to identify, develop, and/or revise patient education materials. Demonstrates flexibility in teaching based on assessment of learner needs and adult learning principles.

cond_0223.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Nurse RN to join our team.
cond_0223.responsibilities:
Clinical advancement
Uses systematic planning, appropriate methods, and timely exchange of information with the multidisciplinary team and patient/family to coordinate care. Manages multiple patient needs and aspects of care. Communicates with the care team to support patient care planning. Uses available resources to problem-solve and determine the most effective approach.
Clinical judgment and decision making
Applies the nursing process and critical thinking to provide patient care that is individualized, goal-directed, and consistent with current safety standards. Identifies actual and potential problems for which the patient is at risk. Evaluates interventions and care on an ongoing basis and adjusts the plan as patient and family needs change. Identifies referral needs based on initial and ongoing assessments. Coordinates with the patient, family, and team members to develop a comprehensive care plan. Prioritizes resource demands and works with others to meet individualized patient needs. Guides other nurses in applying the nursing process with the unit population. Makes appropriate referrals based on assessment findings. Implements safe, therapeutic, and efficient care for patients with complex needs due to multi-system disease or treatment complications. Demonstrates accountability for patient outcomes. Recognizes patient diagnoses even when presenting symptoms vary. Documents per department guidelines, policies, and procedures in a detailed and concise manner. Serves as a resource for other staff on unit-specific documentation. Charting reflects a critical thinking and problem-oriented approach.
Clinical leadership
Delegates and communicates expectations for care delivery to each team member. Understands what can and cannot be delegated to each health care team member. Follows through to confirm delegated tasks are complete. Analyzes each situation before delegating and applies the appropriate level of supervision. Reviews physician orders for appropriateness and raises concerns when needed. Supports coworkers in improving performance. Offers assistance and provides positive feedback. Provides unit-specific information to students, float staff, and travelers, and documents appropriately. Looks for ways to improve work processes and systems. Gives and receives constructive feedback in a non-judgmental and confidential manner.
Nurse-patient/family relationship
Establishes a therapeutic relationship with patients and families. Anticipates barriers to maintaining that relationship and takes steps to address them, including spiritual, cultural, language, or communication barriers. Adapts nursing interventions to meet diverse needs. Acts as a patient advocate by removing obstacles, supporting appropriate needs, and interpreting between patient and physician. Provides age-appropriate patient education covering recovery, self-care, end-of-life care, and health maintenance. Coordinates transfer and discharge planning with other members of the health care team. Works with team members to identify, develop, or revise patient education materials. Adapts teaching based on learner needs and adult learning principles.
cond_0223.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Graduate of nursing school
California Registered Nurse (RN) license — CA Board of Registered Nursing
AHA Basic Life Support for Healthcare Professionals (AHA BLS Healthcare) — American Heart Association
NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS) certification — must be obtained within 90 days of hire
1 Year of clinical experience (RNs with less than 12 months experience will complete new grad requirements)
Preferred Requirements
1 Or more years of hospital clinical RN patient care experience
Independently performs the nursing process through individualized assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation of safe, therapeutic, and efficient care across the continuum, per unit standards. Performs safe nursing care in complex situations with some assistance and supervision. Demonstrates competency in all unit skills and some advanced skills. May teach skills competencies. Coordinates patient care delivered by other care team members. May serve as relief charge nurse and assist with preceptorship or professional development of new nurses and students. Uses common equipment and medications safely and consults others when unfamiliar. Recognizes inconsistencies in patient care and manages potential complications. Maintains consistent organization and prioritization of workload, including confident management of emergency situations. Participates in quality improvement initiatives. Complies with all regulatory and accreditation standards. Demonstrates professional behavior through participation in unit activities and committees as appropriate. Uses a variety of teaching and coaching strategies to support families through the disease process. Promotes clinical effectiveness, efficient use of resources, and quality care. Transfers knowledge and mentors others to improve clinical practice. Demonstrates complex problem solving and critical thinking skills.

cond_0224.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Nurse RN to join our team.
cond_0224.responsibilities:
Essential Functions**
Clinical advancement: Own systematic planning, apply appropriate methods, and drive timely exchange of information with the multidisciplinary team and patient/family to coordinate care. Manage multiple patient needs and aspects of care simultaneously. Lead communication with the care team to direct patient care planning. Apply available resources to determine the most effective course of action.
Clinical judgment and decision making: Execute the nursing process and a critical thinking approach to deliver patient care that incorporates the mind, body and spirit; is individualized, goal directed, and consistent with current standards of safety. Identify actual/potential problems for which the patient is at risk. Continuously evaluate interventions and care, and adjust the plan as patient and family needs change. Determine need for referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Lead collaboration with patient, family and other team members to develop a comprehensive plan of care. Prioritize demand for resources and direct efforts to meet individualized patient needs. Act as preceptor/teacher in guiding other nurses on how to apply the nursing process with a particular unit population. Execute safe, therapeutic and efficient care for patients with complex needs due to multi-system disease and/or complications of treatment. Take accountability for achieving patient outcomes. Quickly recognize a patient diagnosis even when presenting symptoms or situations may be dissimilar. Document per department/entity guidelines of care and policies and procedures — comprehensive, representing a detailed, concise picture of patient's care. Serve as a resource for other staff in managing unit-specific documentation issues. Ensure charting reflects a critical thinking/problem-oriented approach to patient issues.
Clinical leadership: Delegate/assign and communicate expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Maintain knowledge of what can and cannot be delegated to each health care team member. Take responsibility for delegation and follow through to ensure delegated tasks are complete. Before delegating, analyze each situation, determine and consistently apply the appropriate level of supervision needed. Assess appropriateness of physician orders and question the physician when appropriate. Help coworkers improve performance. Offer assistance and support to coworkers. Provide positive feedback to others. Deliver unit-specific information to students, floats, and travelers/registry personnel and document appropriately. Provide incidental teaching to members of the team. Identify and apply ways to improve work processes and systems. Offer and accept constructive feedback/criticism in a non-judgmental, positive and confidential manner.
Nurse-patient/family relationship: Establish a therapeutic relationship with patient and family. Anticipate problems in establishing/maintaining a therapeutic relationship with a specific patient and take actions to enhance the quality of nurse/patient/family interaction (problems may include: spiritual, cultural, language or other communication barriers; those imposed by the nature of illness or health issue). Analyze social/cultural variables and adapt nursing interventions to meet diverse needs. Serve as a patient advocate by removing obstacles, identifying and supporting appropriate needs and wants, and interpreting for patient to physician and vice versa. Deliver age-appropriate patient education that facilitates recovery, self-care, end-of-life care, health maintenance, health promotion, and wellness. Direct transfer and discharge planning and teaching in collaboration with other members of the health care team. Collaborate with other team members to identify, develop and/or revise patient education materials. Demonstrate flexibility in teaching based on assessment of learner's needs and the integration of adult learning principles.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**
Independently execute the nursing process through individualized assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of safe, therapeutic, efficient care for patients with overt and subtle needs throughout the continuum of care, and according to unit's standards of care. Deliver safe nursing care for patients in more complex situations with some assistance and supervision. Demonstrate competency in all areas of unit skills and some advanced skills. May teach some skills competencies. Direct patient care administered by other members of the care team. May assume the responsibility of relief charge nurse and may assist with preceptorship/professional development of new nurses and students. Use common equipment and medications safely in the practice setting and consult others when unfamiliar. Recognize inconsistencies in patient care and manage potential complications. Demonstrate consistent organization and prioritization of workload; confident management of emergency situations. Participate in quality improvement initiatives. Comply with all regulatory and accreditation standards. Demonstrate professional behavior through participation in unit activities and committees as appropriate. Delegate/assign and communicate expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Teach skills as necessary. Coordinate patient care administered by other members of the nursing staff. Apply a variety of teaching/coaching strategies to assist family through disease process/experience. Promote clinical effectiveness, efficient use of resources, and quality care in the practice setting. Transfer knowledge and mentor others to improve clinical practice. Demonstrate complex problem solving and the use of critical thinking skills.

Graduate of nursing school
California Registered Nurse (RN) licensure — CA Board of Registered Nursing
AHA Basic Life Support for Healthcare Professional (AHA BLS Healthcare) — American Heart Association

cond_0257.intro: We are looking for someone to join our team in this role. Most people become stronger in this kind of clinical nursing work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.
cond_0257.responsibilities:
Clinical advancement Uses systematic planning, appropriate methods and timely exchange of information with multidisciplinary team and patient/family to coordinate care. Demonstrates ability to focus on and manage multiple patient needs and aspects of care. Actively communicates with care team to plan patient care. Utilizes available resources to problem-solve and determine most effective approach to action. Clinical judgment and decision making Utilizes the nursing process and a critical thinking approach to provide patient care that incorporates the mind, body and spirit; is individualized, goal directed, and consistent with current standards of safety. Identifies actual/potential problems for which the patient is at risk. Continuously evaluates interventions and care, and adjusts the plan as patient and family needs change. Identifies need for referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Collaborates with patient, family and other team members to develop a comprehensive plan of care. Prioritizes demand for resources and collaborates with others to meet individualized patient needs. Acts as preceptor/teacher in guiding other nurses on how to apply the nursing process with a particular unit population. Makes appropriate referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Implements safe, therapeutic and efficient care for patients with complex needs due to multi-system disease and/or complications of treatment. Demonstrates accountability for achieving patient outcomes. Demonstrates an ability to quickly recognize a patient diagnosis even though presenting symptoms or situations may be dissimilar. Documents per department/entity guidelines of care and policies and procedures. Comprehensive; representing detailed, concise picture of patient's care. Serves as a resource for other staff in managing unit specific documentation issues. Charting reflects a critical thinking/problem oriented approach to patient issues. Clinical leadership Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Knowledgeable about what can and cannot be delegated to each different health care team member. Responsible for delegation and follows through to ensure delegated task is complete. Before delegating, analyzes each situation, determines and consistently applies levels of supervision needed (unsupervised, initial direction and periodic inspection, continuous supervision, or should not be delegated). Assesses appropriateness of physician orders and to question physician when appropriate. Helps coworkers improve performance. Offers assistance and support to coworkers. Provides positive feedback to others. Provides unit specific information to students, floats, travelers/registry personnel and documents appropriately. Provides incidental teaching to members of the team. Looks for and applies ways to improve work processes and systems. Offers and accepts constructive feedback/criticism in a non-judgmental, positive and confidential manner. Seeks out opportunities to assist and support coworkers. Nurse-patient/family relationship Establishes a therapeutic relationship with patient and family. Anticipates problems to establishing/maintaining a therapeutic relationship with a specific patient and takes actions to enhance quality of nurse/patient/family interaction (problems may include: spiritual, cultural, language or other communication barriers; those imposed by nature of illness or health issue). Analyzes social/cultural variables and adapts nursing interventions to meet diverse needs. Serves as a patient advocate through actions such as: removing obstacles, identifying and supporting appropriate needs and wants; interpreting for patient to physician and visa/versa. Provides age appropriate patient education that facilitates recovery, self-care, end-of-life care and health maintenance, health promotion, and wellness. Coordinates transfer and discharge planning and teaching in collaboration with other members of the health care team. Collaborates with other team members to identify, develop and/or revise patient education materials. Demonstrates flexibility to teaching based on assessment of learner's needs and the integration of adult learning principles.
Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities
Independently performs the nursing process through individualized assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of safe, therapeutic, efficient care for patients with overt and subtle needs throughout the continuum of care, and according to unit's standards of care. Performs safe nursing care for patients in more complex situations with some assistance and supervision. Demonstrates competency in all areas of the unit skills and some advanced skills. May teach some skills competencies. Coordinates patient care administered by other members of the care team. May assume the responsibility of relief charge nurse and may assist with preceptorship/professional development of new nurses and students. Uses common equipment and medications safely in the practice setting and consults others when unfamiliar. Recognizes inconsistencies in patient care and manages potential complications. Demonstrates consistent organization and prioritization of workload; confident management of emergency situations. Participates in quality improvement initiatives. Complies with all regulatory and accreditation standards. Demonstrates professional behavior through participation in unit activities and committees as appropriate. Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Teaches skills as necessary. Coordinates patient care administered by other members of the nursing staff. Utilizes a variety of teaching/coaching strategies to assist family through disease process/experience. Promotes clinical effectiveness, efficient use of resources, and quality care in practice setting. Transfers knowledge and mentors others to improve clinical practice. Demonstrates complex problem solving and the use of critical thinking skills.
cond_0257.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Graduate of nursing school
California Registered Nurse (RN) - CA Board of Registered Nursing
AHA Basic Life Support for Healthcare Professional (AHA BLS Healthcare) - American Heart Association
NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS) - Various-Employee provides certificate (required within 90 days of hire)
1 Year clinical experience (RNs with less than 12 months experience will complete the new grad requirements)

cond_0258.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Nurse RN to join our team.
cond_0258.responsibilities:
Clinical advancement
Stays in regular contact with the multidisciplinary team and patient/family to coordinate care using systematic planning, appropriate methods, and timely exchange of information. Actively communicates with the care team throughout the day to plan and adjust patient care. Manages multiple patient needs at once and connects with available resources to determine the most effective approach.
Clinical judgment and decision making
Applies the nursing process and critical thinking to provide individualized, goal-directed patient care consistent with current safety standards. Identifies actual and potential problems, continuously evaluates interventions, and adjusts the plan as patient and family needs change. Collaborates daily with patients, families, and team members to develop and maintain a comprehensive care plan. Initiates referrals based on initial and ongoing assessments. Implements safe, therapeutic, and efficient care for patients with complex, multi-system needs. Maintains thorough, concise documentation that reflects a critical thinking approach and serves as a resource for other staff on documentation issues.
Clinical leadership
Delegates and clearly communicates care delivery expectations to each team member. Analyzes each situation before delegating and applies the appropriate level of supervision. Questions physician orders when appropriate and actively supports coworkers by offering assistance, positive feedback, and constructive input. Shares unit-specific information with students, float staff, and travelers. Looks for ways to improve work processes and brings those ideas forward to the team.
Nurse-patient/family relationship
Builds and maintains a therapeutic relationship with patients and families, anticipating barriers such as cultural, spiritual, language, or illness-related challenges and taking steps to address them. Advocates for patients by removing obstacles, interpreting between patient and physician, and supporting appropriate needs. Provides age-appropriate patient education covering recovery, self-care, end-of-life care, and health promotion. Coordinates transfer and discharge planning in collaboration with the broader care team. Adapts teaching approaches based on learner needs and adult learning principles.

California Registered Nurse (RN) license from the CA Board of Registered Nursing
AHA Basic Life Support for Healthcare Professionals (AHA BLS Healthcare) — American Heart Association

1 Year of clinical experience (RNs with less than 12 months experience will complete the new grad requirements)
Preferred Requirements

Utilizes available resources to problem-solve and determine most effective approach to action. Clinical judgment and decision making Utilizes the nursing process and a critical thinking approach to provide patient care that incorporates the mind, body and spirit; is individualized, goal directed, and consistent with current standards of safety. Identifies actual/potential problems for which the patient is at risk. Continuously evaluates interventions and care, and adjusts the plan as patient and family needs change. Identifies need for referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Collaborates with patient, family and other team members to develop a comprehensive plan of care. Prioritizes demand for resources and collaborates with others to meet individualized patient needs. Acts as preceptor/teacher in guiding other nurses on how to apply the nursing process with a particular unit population. Makes appropriate referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Implements safe, therapeutic and efficient care for patients with complex needs due to multi-system disease and/or complications of treatment. Demonstrates accountability for achieving patient outcomes. Demonstrates an ability to quickly recognize a patient diagnosis even though presenting symptoms or situations may be dissimilar. Documents per department/entity guidelines of care and policies and procedures. Comprehensive; representing detailed, concise picture of patient's care. Serves as a resource for other staff in managing unit specific documentation issues. Charting reflects a critical thinking/problem oriented approach to patient issues. Uses common equipment and medications safely in the practice setting and consults others when unfamiliar. Recognizes inconsistencies in patient care and manages potential complications. Complies with all regulatory and accreditation standards. Demonstrates professional behavior through participation in unit activities and committees as appropriate. Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Teaches skills as necessary. Coordinates patient care administered by other members of the nursing staff. Utilizes a variety of teaching/coaching strategies to assist family through disease process/experience. Promotes clinical effectiveness, efficient use of resources, and quality care in practice setting. Transfers knowledge and mentors others to improve clinical practice. Demonstrates complex problem solving and the use of critical thinking skills.

Stays in regular contact with the multidisciplinary team and patient/family to coordinate care using systematic planning, appropriate methods, and timely exchange of information. Actively communicates with the care team throughout the day to plan and adjust patient care. Manages multiple patient needs at once and connects with available resources to determine the most effective approach.
Clinical judgment and decision making
Applies the nursing process and critical thinking to provide individualized, goal-directed patient care consistent with current safety standards. Identifies actual and potential problems, continuously evaluates interventions, and adjusts the plan as patient and family needs change. Collaborates daily with patients, families, and team members to develop and maintain a comprehensive care plan. Initiates referrals based on initial and ongoing assessments. Implements safe, therapeutic, and efficient care for patients with complex, multi-system needs. Maintains thorough, concise documentation that reflects a critical thinking approach and serves as a resource for other staff on documentation issues.
Clinical leadership
Delegates and clearly communicates care delivery expectations to each team member. Analyzes each situation before delegating and applies the appropriate level of supervision. Advocates for patients by removing obstacles, interpreting between patient and physician, and supporting appropriate needs. Provides age-appropriate patient education covering recovery, self-care, end-of-life care, and health promotion. Coordinates transfer and discharge planning in collaboration with the broader care team. Adapts teaching approaches based on learner needs and adult learning principles.

cond_0285.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Nurse RN to join our team.
cond_0285.responsibilities:
Clinical advancement
Uses systematic planning, appropriate methods, and regular exchange of information with the multidisciplinary team and patient/family to coordinate care. Actively communicates with the care team daily to plan patient care. Demonstrates ability to focus on and manage multiple patient needs and aspects of care. Utilizes available resources to problem-solve and determine the most effective approach.
Clinical judgment and decision making
Utilizes the nursing process and a critical thinking approach to provide patient care that incorporates the mind, body, and spirit; is individualized, goal directed, and consistent with current standards of safety. Identifies actual/potential problems for which the patient is at risk. Continuously evaluates interventions and care, and adjusts the plan as patient and family needs change. Identifies need for referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Collaborates closely with the patient, family, and other team members to develop a comprehensive plan of care. Prioritizes demand for resources and works with others to meet individualized patient needs. Acts as preceptor/teacher in guiding other nurses on how to apply the nursing process with a particular unit population. Implements safe, therapeutic, and efficient care for patients with complex needs due to multi-system disease and/or complications of treatment. Demonstrates accountability for achieving patient outcomes. Demonstrates an ability to quickly recognize a patient diagnosis even though presenting symptoms or situations may be dissimilar. Documents per department/entity guidelines of care and policies and procedures; charting reflects a critical thinking/problem-oriented approach to patient issues. Serves as a resource for other staff in managing unit-specific documentation issues.
Clinical leadership
Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Knowledgeable about what can and cannot be delegated to each different health care team member. Responsible for delegation and follows through to ensure delegated tasks are complete. Before delegating, analyzes each situation and consistently applies appropriate levels of supervision. Assesses appropriateness of physician orders and speaks up to question the physician when appropriate. Helps coworkers improve performance. Offers assistance and support to coworkers. Provides positive feedback to others. Provides unit-specific information to students, floats, and travelers/registry personnel. Provides incidental teaching to members of the team. Looks for and applies ways to improve work processes and systems. Offers and accepts constructive feedback in a non-judgmental, positive, and confidential manner.
Nurse-patient/family relationship
Establishes a therapeutic relationship with patients and families through regular, ongoing interaction. Anticipates problems in establishing or maintaining a therapeutic relationship and takes actions to enhance the quality of nurse/patient/family interaction. Analyzes social/cultural variables and adapts nursing interventions to meet diverse needs. Serves as a patient advocate by removing obstacles, identifying and supporting appropriate needs and wants, and interpreting between patient and physician. Provides age-appropriate patient education that facilitates recovery, self-care, end-of-life care, and health maintenance. Coordinates transfer and discharge planning and teaching in collaboration with other members of the health care team. Collaborates with other team members to identify, develop, and/or revise patient education materials. Demonstrates flexibility in teaching based on assessment of learner needs and adult learning principles.

Clinical advancement: Uses systematic planning, appropriate methods, and timely exchange of information with the multidisciplinary team and patient/family to coordinate care. Demonstrates ability to focus on and manage multiple patient needs and aspects of care. Actively communicates with the care team to plan patient care. Works with available resources to determine the most effective approach to action.
Clinical judgment and decision making: Works within the nursing process and a critical thinking approach to provide patient care that incorporates the mind, body, and spirit; is individualized, goal directed, and consistent with current standards of safety. Identifies actual/potential problems for which the patient is at risk. Continuously evaluates interventions and care, and adjusts the plan as patient and family needs change. Identifies need for referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Collaborates with patient, family, and other team members to develop a comprehensive plan of care. Coordinates demand for resources and works with others to meet individualized patient needs. Supports other nurses by guiding them on how to apply the nursing process with a particular unit population. Makes appropriate referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Helps deliver safe, therapeutic, and efficient care for patients with complex needs due to multi-system disease and/or complications of treatment. Shares accountability for achieving patient outcomes. Demonstrates an ability to quickly recognize a patient diagnosis even though presenting symptoms or situations may be dissimilar. Documents per department/entity guidelines of care and policies and procedures. Charting is comprehensive, representing a detailed, concise picture of patient care. Serves as a resource for other staff in managing unit-specific documentation issues. Charting reflects a critical thinking/problem-oriented approach to patient issues.
Clinical leadership: Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Knowledgeable about what can and cannot be delegated to each different health care team member. Responsible for delegation and follows through to ensure delegated tasks are complete. Before delegating, analyzes each situation and consistently applies appropriate levels of supervision. Assesses appropriateness of physician orders and raises questions with the physician when appropriate. Helps coworkers improve performance. Offers assistance and support to coworkers. Provides positive feedback to others. Shares unit-specific information with students, floats, travelers/registry personnel and documents appropriately. Provides incidental teaching to members of the team. Looks for and applies ways to improve work processes and systems. Offers and accepts constructive feedback/criticism in a non-judgmental, positive, and confidential manner. Seeks out opportunities to assist and support coworkers.
Nurse-patient/family relationship: Establishes a therapeutic relationship with patient and family. Anticipates problems in establishing/maintaining a therapeutic relationship with a specific patient and takes actions to enhance the quality of nurse/patient/family interaction (problems may include: spiritual, cultural, language, or other communication barriers; those imposed by nature of illness or health issue). Analyzes social/cultural variables and adapts nursing interventions to meet diverse needs. Serves as a patient advocate through actions such as: removing obstacles, identifying and supporting appropriate needs and wants; interpreting for patient to physician and vice versa. Provides age-appropriate patient education that facilitates recovery, self-care, end-of-life care, and health maintenance, health promotion, and wellness. Coordinates transfer and discharge planning and teaching in collaboration with other members of the health care team. Works with other team members to identify, develop, and/or revise patient education materials. Demonstrates flexibility in teaching based on assessment of learner needs and the integration of adult learning principles.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**
Independently performs the nursing process through individualized assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation of safe, therapeutic, efficient care for patients with overt and subtle needs throughout the continuum of care, and according to unit standards of care. Performs safe nursing care for patients in more complex situations with some assistance and supervision. Demonstrates competency in all areas of unit skills and some advanced skills. May teach some skills competencies. Coordinates patient care administered by other members of the care team. May assume the responsibility of relief charge nurse and may assist with preceptorship/professional development of new nurses and students. Uses common equipment and medications safely in the practice setting and consults others when unfamiliar. Recognizes inconsistencies in patient care and manages potential complications. Demonstrates consistent organization and prioritization of workload; confident management of emergency situations. Participates in quality improvement initiatives. Complies with all regulatory and accreditation standards. Demonstrates professional behavior through participation in unit activities and committees as appropriate. Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Teaches skills as necessary. Coordinates patient care administered by other members of the nursing staff. Utilizes a variety of teaching/coaching strategies to assist family through disease process/experience. Promotes clinical effectiveness, efficient use of resources, and quality care in practice setting. Transfers knowledge and mentors others to improve clinical practice. Demonstrates complex problem solving and the use of critical thinking skills.
cond_0297.requirements:
Minimum Requirements**
Graduate of nursing school
California Registered Nurse (RN) license from CA Board of Registered Nursing
AHA Basic Life Support for Healthcare Professional (AHA BLS Healthcare) - American Heart Association
NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS) certification (within 90 days of hire)
1 Year of clinical experience (RNs with less than 12 months experience will complete the new grad requirements)
Preferred Requirements**
1 Or more years of related hospital clinical RN patient care experience

Clinical judgment and decision making
Utilizes the nursing process and a critical thinking approach to provide patient care that incorporates the mind, body, and spirit; is individualized, goal directed, and consistent with current standards of safety. Identifies need for referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Implements safe, therapeutic, and efficient care for patients with complex needs due to multi-system disease and/or complications of treatment. Demonstrates accountability for achieving patient outcomes. Demonstrates an ability to quickly recognize a patient diagnosis even though presenting symptoms or situations may be dissimilar. cond_0327.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Nurse RN to join our team.
cond_0327.responsibilities:
What You Will Do**
To provide direct and indirect nursing services to patients and families.
Essential Functions**
Clinical advancement Uses systematic planning, appropriate methods and timely exchange of information with multidisciplinary team and patient/family to coordinate care. Demonstrates ability to focus on and manage multiple patient needs and aspects of care. Actively communicates with care team to plan patient care. Utilizes available resources to problem-solve and determine most effective approach to action. Clinical judgment and decision making Utilizes the nursing process and a critical thinking approach to provide patient care that incorporates the mind, body and spirit; is individualized, goal directed, and consistent with current standards of safety. Identifies actual/potential problems for which the patient is at risk. Continuously evaluates interventions and care, and adjusts the plan as patient and family needs change. Identifies need for referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Collaborates with patient, family and other team members to develop a comprehensive plan of care. Prioritizes demand for resources and collaborates with others to meet individualized patient needs. Acts as preceptor/teacher in guiding other nurses on how to apply the nursing process with a particular unit population. Makes appropriate referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Implements safe, therapeutic and efficient care for patients with complex needs due to multi-system disease and/or complications of treatment. Demonstrates accountability for achieving patient outcomes. Demonstrates an ability to quickly recognize a patient diagnosis even though presenting symptoms or situations may be dissimilar. Documents per department/entity guidelines of care and policies and procedures. Comprehensive; representing detailed, concise picture of patient's care. Serves as a resource for other staff in managing unit specific documentation issues. Charting reflects a critical thinking/problem oriented approach to patient issues. Clinical leadership Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Knowledgeable about what can and cannot be delegated to each different health care team member. Responsible for delegation and follows through to ensure delegated task is complete. Before delegating, analyzes each situation, determines and consistently applies levels of supervision needed (unsupervised, initial direction and periodic inspection, continuous supervision, or should not be delegated). Assesses appropriateness of physician orders and to question physician when appropriate. Helps coworkers improve performance. Offers assistance and support to coworkers. Provides positive feedback to others. Provides unit specific information to students, floats, travelers/registry personnel and documents appropriately. Anticipates problems to establishing/maintaining a therapeutic relationship with a specific patient and takes actions to enhance quality of nurse/patient/family interaction (problems may include: spiritual, cultural, language or other communication barriers; those imposed by nature of illness or health issue). Analyzes social/cultural variables and adapts nursing interventions to meet diverse needs. Serves as a patient advocate through actions such as: removing obstacles, identifying and supporting appropriate needs and wants; interpreting for patient to physician and visa/versa. Provides age appropriate patient education that facilitates recovery, self-care, end-of-life care and health maintenance, health promotion, and wellness. Coordinates transfer and discharge planning and teaching in collaboration with other members of the health care team. Collaborates with other team members to identify, develop and/or revise patient education materials. Demonstrates flexibility to teaching based on assessment of learner's needs and the integration of adult learning principles.

Independently performs the nursing process through individualized assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of safe, therapeutic, efficient care for patients with overt and subtle needs throughout the continuum of care, and according to unit's standards of care. Performs safe nursing care for patients in more complex situations with some assistance and supervision. Demonstrates competency in all areas of the unit skills and some advanced skills. May teach some skills competencies. Coordinates patient care administered by other members of the care team. May assume the responsibility of relief charge nurse and may assist with preceptorship/professional development of new nurses and students. Uses common equipment and medications safely in the practice setting and consults others when unfamiliar. Recognizes inconsistencies in patient care and manages potential complications. Demonstrates consistent organization and prioritization of workload; confident management of emergency situations. Participates in quality improvement initiatives. Complies with all regulatory and accreditation standards. Demonstrates professional behavior through participation in unit activities and committees as appropriate. Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Teaches skills as necessary. Coordinates patient care administered by other members of the nursing staff. Utilizes a variety of teaching/coaching strategies to assist family through disease process/experience. Demonstrates complex problem solving and the use of critical thinking skills.

cond_0339.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Nurse RN to join our team.
cond_0339.responsibilities:
Clinical advancement
Uses systematic planning, appropriate methods, and regular exchange of information with the multidisciplinary team and patient/family to coordinate care. Actively communicates with the care team daily to plan patient care. Demonstrates ability to focus on and manage multiple patient needs and aspects of care. Utilizes available resources to problem-solve and determine the most effective approach.
Clinical judgment and decision making
Utilizes the nursing process and a critical thinking approach to provide patient care that incorporates the mind, body, and spirit; is individualized, goal directed, and consistent with current standards of safety. Identifies actual/potential problems for which the patient is at risk. Continuously evaluates interventions and care, and adjusts the plan as patient and family needs change. Identifies need for referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Collaborates closely with the patient, family, and other team members to develop a comprehensive plan of care. Prioritizes demand for resources and works with others to meet individualized patient needs. Acts as preceptor/teacher in guiding other nurses on how to apply the nursing process with a particular unit population. Implements safe, therapeutic, and efficient care for patients with complex needs due to multi-system disease and/or complications of treatment. Demonstrates accountability for achieving patient outcomes. Demonstrates an ability to quickly recognize a patient diagnosis even though presenting symptoms or situations may be dissimilar. Documents per department/entity guidelines of care and policies and procedures; charting reflects a critical thinking/problem-oriented approach to patient issues. Serves as a resource for other staff in managing unit-specific documentation issues.
Clinical leadership
Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Knowledgeable about what can and cannot be delegated to each different health care team member. Responsible for delegation and follows through to ensure delegated tasks are complete. Before delegating, analyzes each situation and consistently applies appropriate levels of supervision. Assesses appropriateness of physician orders and speaks up to question the physician when appropriate. Helps coworkers improve performance. Offers assistance and support to coworkers. Provides positive feedback to others. Provides unit-specific information to students, floats, and travelers/registry personnel. Provides incidental teaching to members of the team. Looks for and applies ways to improve work processes and systems. Offers and accepts constructive feedback in a non-judgmental, positive, and confidential manner.
Nurse-patient/family relationship
Establishes a therapeutic relationship with patients and families through regular, ongoing interaction. Anticipates problems in establishing or maintaining a therapeutic relationship and takes actions to enhance the quality of nurse/patient/family interaction. Analyzes social/cultural variables and adapts nursing interventions to meet diverse needs. Serves as a patient advocate by removing obstacles, identifying and supporting appropriate needs and wants, and interpreting between patient and physician. Provides age-appropriate patient education that facilitates recovery, self-care, end-of-life care, and health maintenance. Coordinates transfer and discharge planning and teaching in collaboration with other members of the health care team. Collaborates with other team members to identify, develop, and/or revise patient education materials. Demonstrates flexibility in teaching based on assessment of learner needs and adult learning principles.

cond_0351.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Nurse RN to join our team.
cond_0351.responsibilities:
Essential Functions**
Clinical advancement: Uses systematic planning, appropriate methods, and timely exchange of information with the multidisciplinary team and patient/family to coordinate care. Demonstrates ability to focus on and manage multiple patient needs and aspects of care. Actively communicates with the care team to plan patient care. Works with available resources to determine the most effective approach to action.
Clinical judgment and decision making: Works within the nursing process and a critical thinking approach to provide patient care that incorporates the mind, body, and spirit; is individualized, goal directed, and consistent with current standards of safety. Identifies actual/potential problems for which the patient is at risk. Continuously evaluates interventions and care, and adjusts the plan as patient and family needs change. Identifies need for referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Collaborates with patient, family, and other team members to develop a comprehensive plan of care. Coordinates demand for resources and works with others to meet individualized patient needs. Supports other nurses by guiding them on how to apply the nursing process with a particular unit population. Makes appropriate referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Helps deliver safe, therapeutic, and efficient care for patients with complex needs due to multi-system disease and/or complications of treatment. Shares accountability for achieving patient outcomes. Demonstrates an ability to quickly recognize a patient diagnosis even though presenting symptoms or situations may be dissimilar. Documents per department/entity guidelines of care and policies and procedures. Charting is comprehensive, representing a detailed, concise picture of patient care. Serves as a resource for other staff in managing unit-specific documentation issues. Charting reflects a critical thinking/problem-oriented approach to patient issues.
Clinical leadership: Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Knowledgeable about what can and cannot be delegated to each different health care team member. Responsible for delegation and follows through to ensure delegated tasks are complete. Before delegating, analyzes each situation and consistently applies appropriate levels of supervision. Assesses appropriateness of physician orders and raises questions with the physician when appropriate. Helps coworkers improve performance. Offers assistance and support to coworkers. Provides positive feedback to others. Shares unit-specific information with students, floats, travelers/registry personnel and documents appropriately. Provides incidental teaching to members of the team. Looks for and applies ways to improve work processes and systems. Offers and accepts constructive feedback/criticism in a non-judgmental, positive, and confidential manner. Seeks out opportunities to assist and support coworkers.
Nurse-patient/family relationship: Establishes a therapeutic relationship with patient and family. Anticipates problems in establishing/maintaining a therapeutic relationship with a specific patient and takes actions to enhance the quality of nurse/patient/family interaction (problems may include: spiritual, cultural, language, or other communication barriers; those imposed by nature of illness or health issue). Analyzes social/cultural variables and adapts nursing interventions to meet diverse needs. Serves as a patient advocate through actions such as: removing obstacles, identifying and supporting appropriate needs and wants; interpreting for patient to physician and vice versa. Provides age-appropriate patient education that facilitates recovery, self-care, end-of-life care, and health maintenance, health promotion, and wellness. Coordinates transfer and discharge planning and teaching in collaboration with other members of the health care team. Works with other team members to identify, develop, and/or revise patient education materials. Demonstrates flexibility in teaching based on assessment of learner needs and the integration of adult learning principles.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**
Independently performs the nursing process through individualized assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation of safe, therapeutic, efficient care for patients with overt and subtle needs throughout the continuum of care, and according to unit standards of care. Performs safe nursing care for patients in more complex situations with some assistance and supervision. Demonstrates competency in all areas of unit skills and some advanced skills. May teach some skills competencies. Coordinates patient care administered by other members of the care team. May assume the responsibility of relief charge nurse and may assist with preceptorship/professional development of new nurses and students. Uses common equipment and medications safely in the practice setting and consults others when unfamiliar. Recognizes inconsistencies in patient care and manages potential complications. Demonstrates consistent organization and prioritization of workload; confident management of emergency situations. Participates in quality improvement initiatives. Complies with all regulatory and accreditation standards. Demonstrates professional behavior through participation in unit activities and committees as appropriate. Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Teaches skills as necessary. Coordinates patient care administered by other members of the nursing staff. Utilizes a variety of teaching/coaching strategies to assist family through disease process/experience. Promotes clinical effectiveness, efficient use of resources, and quality care in practice setting. Transfers knowledge and mentors others to improve clinical practice. Demonstrates complex problem solving and the use of critical thinking skills.
cond_0351.requirements:
Minimum Requirements**
Graduate of nursing school
California Registered Nurse (RN) license from CA Board of Registered Nursing
AHA Basic Life Support for Healthcare Professional (AHA BLS Healthcare) - American Heart Association
NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS) certification (within 90 days of hire)
1 Year of clinical experience (RNs with less than 12 months experience will complete the new grad requirements)
Preferred Requirements**
1 Or more years of related hospital clinical RN patient care experience

cond_0357.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Nurse RN to join our team.
cond_0357.responsibilities:
Clinical advancement
Uses systematic planning, appropriate methods, and regular exchange of information with the multidisciplinary team and patient/family to coordinate care. Actively communicates with the care team daily to plan patient care. Demonstrates ability to focus on and manage multiple patient needs and aspects of care. Utilizes available resources to problem-solve and determine the most effective approach.
Clinical judgment and decision making
Utilizes the nursing process and a critical thinking approach to provide patient care that incorporates the mind, body, and spirit; is individualized, goal directed, and consistent with current standards of safety. Identifies actual/potential problems for which the patient is at risk. Continuously evaluates interventions and care, and adjusts the plan as patient and family needs change. Identifies need for referrals based on information obtained in initial and ongoing assessments and evaluation. Collaborates closely with the patient, family, and other team members to develop a comprehensive plan of care. Prioritizes demand for resources and works with others to meet individualized patient needs. Acts as preceptor/teacher in guiding other nurses on how to apply the nursing process with a particular unit population. Implements safe, therapeutic, and efficient care for patients with complex needs due to multi-system disease and/or complications of treatment. Demonstrates accountability for achieving patient outcomes. Demonstrates an ability to quickly recognize a patient diagnosis even though presenting symptoms or situations may be dissimilar. Documents per department/entity guidelines of care and policies and procedures; charting reflects a critical thinking/problem-oriented approach to patient issues. Serves as a resource for other staff in managing unit-specific documentation issues.
Clinical leadership
Delegates/assigns and communicates expectations for care delivery processes to each member of the team. Knowledgeable about what can and cannot be delegated to each different health care team member. Responsible for delegation and follows through to ensure delegated tasks are complete. Before delegating, analyzes each situation and consistently applies appropriate levels of supervision. Assesses appropriateness of physician orders and speaks up to question the physician when appropriate. Helps coworkers improve performance. Offers assistance and support to coworkers. Provides positive feedback to others. Provides unit-specific information to students, floats, and travelers/registry personnel. Provides incidental teaching to members of the team. Looks for and applies ways to improve work processes and systems. Offers and accepts constructive feedback in a non-judgmental, positive, and confidential manner.
Nurse-patient/family relationship
Establishes a therapeutic relationship with patients and families through regular, ongoing interaction. Anticipates problems in establishing or maintaining a therapeutic relationship and takes actions to enhance the quality of nurse/patient/family interaction. Analyzes social/cultural variables and adapts nursing interventions to meet diverse needs. Serves as a patient advocate by removing obstacles, identifying and supporting appropriate needs and wants, and interpreting between patient and physician. Provides age-appropriate patient education that facilitates recovery, self-care, end-of-life care, and health maintenance. Coordinates transfer and discharge planning and teaching in collaboration with other members of the health care team. Collaborates with other team members to identify, develop, and/or revise patient education materials. Demonstrates flexibility in teaching based on assessment of learner needs and adult learning principles.
